As we look ahead to one week, the interval expands to [60.36, 64.04], accounting for more potential variability. While these intervals represent a 90% confidence level, meaning there's a 10% chance the actual outcome will fall outside this range, certain unforeseen events could dramatically push results beyond these bounds. On the upside, an unexpected positive catalyst such as a significant policy change, a major technological breakthrough, or a sudden surge in underlying demand could drive outcomes higher than the 66.18 mark. Conversely, the downside risks include a sudden economic shock, a major geopolitical event, an unforeseen regulatory crackdown, or a severe disruptive incident that fundamentally alters the operating environment. These "black swan" events, by their nature, are difficult to predict but have the potential to cause outcomes to diverge significantly from even the broadest part of the forecasted range.
